turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Come on back, room three is open. What brings you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It's nothing. My wife made me come. Face looks a little off, that's all.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Alright. The nurse will grab vitals and the doctor will be right in.
[SEG0004] person_3 (NURSE): Hey. I'm just getting a pressure and a pulse real quick. My sister woke up with a droopy face a couple years ago, whole family panicked, and hers cleared up fine.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): See? It'll pass. I almost stayed home.
[SEG0006] person_3 (NURSE): Pressure is one twenty eight over seventy eight. Pulse 76. Oxygen sat ninety eight percent. You feeling okay?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm fine. Little tired maybe, but that's just work.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hi, I'm Dr. Shah. Sounds like the face changed overnight?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Not a big deal. I woke up and the left side was kinda droopy. I can still talk and all.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): When did you first notice the droop?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I slept fine. I don't drink much, maybe a beer on the weekend. Work's been nuts though.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. The face though, what time this morning?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh, mirror at like six thirty. Wasn't like that last night.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Can you close the left eye all the way?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really. It just hangs open a bit. Annoying, not painful.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): What about whistling?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Can't whistle at all. Smile looks dumb. Whatever.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any weakness in the arm or the leg?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): The ear was a little sore yesterday. It's gone. I don't get the fuss.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay, the ear. I'm asking about the arm. Does it feel weak?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Arm's normal. Took the trash out this morning.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any trouble with speech, slurring, wrong words?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Talking fine.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Headache, dizziness, or double vision?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Nope. None of that.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): The ear, which side, and is the pain actually gone?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Left ear, kinda behind it. Yesterday afternoon. Nothing today. I took a couple Advil and forgot it.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): What medicines do you take on a regular basis?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): A water pill every morning for my pressure, twenty five milligrams. And the purple inhaler if my chest gets tight.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you know the name of the water pill?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, hydrochlorthiazide I think. Yeah that.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Purple inhaler, that's Advair?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah Advair. Couple puffs, maybe twice a week. Not daily.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any reactions to drugs, rashes, swelling, anything like that?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, there was a rash years ago. Maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which. I don't really remember.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Raise your eyebrows.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right forehead wrinkles. Left side doesn't move at all.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah it looks weird. It's mild though.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Close tight. Left eye still shows some white, it won't seal. Now smile. The mouth pulls over to the right.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Grip my fingers. Both arms are strong and equal. Your speech is clear, no slurring.

[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking out loud. Forehead plus the eye plus the mouth means the facial nerve itself, not a stroke in the brain. That nerve gets inflamed, usually after a virus, and swells in a tight bony canal so the signals don't get through. I'm calling this Bell's palsy for now.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): So not a stroke. Then I really don't need all this.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): It's still the nerve and we treat it early. I want prednisone, sixty milligrams by mouth once a day for five days, then ten milligrams less each day.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Sixty? That's a lot for something that'll just go away.

[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): It feels like a lot, I know. It brings the swelling down on the nerve. The eye can't close so it'll dry out. Use artificial tears every two hours while you're awake, and at night tape the eye shut with some ointment.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Tape. Seriously?
[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yeah seriously. If the eye gets red, painful, or the vision blurs, don't wait. Otherwise I'll see you back in one week to check the face.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. One week. Can I work?
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): You can work, just no dust in that eye. Reception will book the week and send the prednisone to your pharmacy.
[SEG0050] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll put you down for next week and send the script. You all set?
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah I'm good.

spec.situation: Person woke with one side of the face drooping, cannot close the eye, cannot whistle; no arm weakness, no speech problem, ear pain a day before; doctor examines and starts steroids, eye care explained.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
